Solutions 1 and 3 give 57/63 and 61/68 isomorphism classes, which look far too large. I could not derive or verify the exact counts here, so this is a plausibility judgment rather than a check.

Many rod and layer groups that differ geometrically are abstractly the same group, for example direct products such as Z × (point group). Because of this, the abstract classes should collapse much more strongly than the 230 → 219 reduction for 3D space groups. The counts of 57 or 61 for rod groups would leave almost no collapse from 75, which is implausible.

Solution 2's pair (33, 47) is the most plausible of the three, though I am not certain it is exactly right.

CHOICE: 2
